Commentary.Commentary: Phew! So that is it from us for this Test. Been a historic one to say the least. While South Africa will be over the moon, Australia will need to introspect and come out from this with a clear vision for the future. The series now heads to Adelaide for the Day/Night Test staring on 24th November at 0900 IST and it should be another interesting game. Will the tourists inflict a whitewash or will Australia salvage some pride? Let's wait and see. Hope you liked your coverage, we look forward to your company in the coming games. Until then, it's goodbye and take care!

Victorious South African captain, FAF DU PLESSIS is absolutely happy to put up another great performance. He says all his bowlers were exceptional but has a special mention to Abbott for stepping up at the right time and grabbing the opportunity. Adds that it was Philander who set the tone for them in the first innings. Admits they didn't let the momentum shift and as a result they got the desired result. He wants both AB de Villiers and Dale Steyn to join and celebrate with them as they would know how difficult it is to beat Australia in their own den. Mentions that his aim is to take this South African team to the next level and is proud of the efforts put in. On the Day/Night Test, He says that it would be a different challenge and will be up for it. Ends by saying they have a golden opportunity to beat Australia 3-0 and that's their next mission.

Australian skipper, STEVEN SMITH is disappointed as his team didn't put up a fight. Adds that they didn't play to their strengths again and credits South Africa for outplaying them in the series. Confesses that when the confidence is low, it's really difficult for any team and the best way to win is to spend more time in the middle fighting it out. Praises the bowling efforts of Rabada, Abbott and Philander on this deck. Ends by saying they are working hard and with the series already gone with a match to go, they have nothing to lose and will look to do better in the final Test in Adelaide. On the team changes in the next Test, he says it is all upto the selectors and they surely need to get this team over the line and hopes the Adelaide crowd to be an inspiration for them.

MAN OF THE MATCH, KYLE ABBOTT says that he just loves to make the most of the opportunities given to him. Adds that he wants to keep doing this for his team. Further adds that the sun not coming out helped him with the movement. Informs his idea was to make the batsman play for everything and when the pitch assists, it makes things interesting for him. Adds that they came into the series knowing the strengths and weaknesses of each batsman. Ends by saying the party is on for sure tonight.

Australia would feel like they are in a rut, they have lost five Tests in a row. They struggled against spin in Sri Lanka and now have been outplayed at home by South Africa who have used the moving ball superbly. There will be a lot of tough questions asked and the home side will know they need to answer them and prepare well for the coming games. Testing times ahead. Meanwhile, stay tuned for the presentation.

It has been a memorable Test series for South Africa, they had no Dale Steyn and AB de Villiers yet Faf du Plessis has managed to get the team together and put in one of their finest performances in Test cricket. Kagiso Rabada and Kyle Abbott were the standout bowlers for them with good support from the others as well. Batting shaped up well for them too. To think Hashim Amla and Faf du Plessis did not score a ton yet the tourists found new heroes in Dean Elgar, JP Duminy and also Temba Bavuma who chipped in with vital fifties.

Everything worked for the tourists in this Test, right from the toss. They won the toss, bundled out Australia for 85 and the 144-run stand between de Kock and Bavuma steadied them. Quinton de Kock's ton ensured they got a huge lead of 241 runs and despite a good start for Australia, Kagiso Rabada and Kyle Abbott shared ten wickets between them to wrap things up. Poor Philander who got a five-fer in the first innings, bowled his heart out but could not pick a single wicket in the second. South Africa have played superbly as a team to win their third consecutive Test series against Australia in Australia.

What a collapse for Australia, their second one in the game and South Africa have been ruthless to not just wrap up the Test but also the series with an innings victory. Australia lost eight wickets for a mere 40 runs in just 24.1 overs today. Abbott and Philander did not bowl any boundary balls to begin with and that created the pressure on Australia to start scoring. The frustration built up and out came the indecisive strokes and South Africa just ran through the batting line-up to register their first ever innings victory against Australia in Australia!

OUT! It's all over for Australia! The South African team is in a huddle, they are cherishing the moment. Faf du Plessis is the happiest man on this planet. What a performance from his team to defeat Australia in their own den. Coming to the ball, it was a full ball on the stumps, Lyon backs away and chips it straight to Philander at mid on who takes a comfortable catch. Kyle Abbott is down on his knees and his teammates barge towards him. SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY AN INNINGS AND 80 RUNS AND SEAL THE SERIES WITH A GAME TO GO!
Fuller on the stumps, Josh Hazlewood digs it out in time.
Back of a length delivery on off, Hazlewood backs away and pushes it towards the fielder at mid off.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

FOUR! Edged and through! Hurls it on a length and outside off, Hazlewood pokes at it and almost pays the price for it. Gets an outside edge past the diving Elgar at third slip for a boundary towards third man.

Outside off, way too wide for the Australian skipper to play a shot.
Smith stays in his crease and defends it.

Fuller outside off, Khawaja drives it back to the bowler who collects and throws the ball back to the keeper.
Good length outside off, Smith is opened up a touch and he defends it off the outer half towards covers.
Good length on off, Smith gets across and tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Fuller outside off, Smith comes forward and drives it towards short extra cover who dives and stops the ball.

Back of a length outside off, Khawaja gets across and defends it back down the wicket.

The players are out in the middle with the sun shining on them. Australia will be hoping for a wicket-less first session while the tourists will be wanting a session with too many of them. USMAN KHAWAJA and STEVEN SMITH are out to bat. South Africa begin the day with KYLE ABBOTT. Here we go....

South Africa will feel a touch unlucky? They bowled really well to beat the bat on several occasions yesterday yet could only scalp two wickets. They will hope to begin well today and look to force an innings victory. Will they be able to do it? Or will Australia do a South Africa at W.A.C.A on them? Let's see.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of Day 4 of the second Test between Australia and South Africa at the Bellerive Oval, Hobart. The host have their task cut out, having already lost two wickets and still trail by 120 runs. Their first target will be to ensure that they wipe off the deficit without losing too many and then make South Africa chase a tricky target. That though is a bit too far for now.
DAY 4, SESSION 1....

One would feel the bowling wasn't that good by the visitors if he looks at the scorecard, but that's not the case. Abbott was the one who got both the scalps while Philander and Rabada bowled lovely lines and lengths to trouble the Aussie batsmen. The deficit is still 120 and the home side has its work cut out. Again we have an early start at 0430 IST and let's hope we get another entertaining day of Test cricket tomorrow, of course the weather should be kind. Will Smith and co. come out with a plan to deal with the Protea pacers? Or will the Saffas wrap it up? Join us tomorrow to see how day 4 pans out. Until then, it's goodbye from us. Cheers!

Smith then walked out to the middle and gave good company to Khawaja who has registered another vital fifty under his belt and almost saw off the day before the bad light came into play. Earlier in the day, a stunning ton from Quniton de Kock and a gritty half century from Bavuma allowed the Proteas to stamp their authority firmly on this game as they not only threaded the 144-run stand but also got a huge lead of 241 runs.

That's brings us to the end of another exciting day of Test cricket. Australia will be happy going into the dressing room as they have put up a better show with the bat this time around. After bundling out South Africa for 326, they didn't get the best of the starts as Joe Burns was shown the way to the pavilion in the very first over by Abbott. Warner and Khawaja then steadied the ship although they survived a few scares but compiled a crucial 79-run stand before the former got out in an unfortunate way.
Right then, this was on the cards. It had gone dark out there and that left the umpires with no other option. STUMPS ON DAY 3!
The players are going off. Light has faded a lot and the umpires have stopped play. Not stumps yet officially, but don't see light improving now. Stay tuned.
Looks to tuck it to the leg side but the ball goes off the inside edge through square leg and the batsmen take a run.

Fuller in length and angling in, Smith comes across and flicks it through wide mid on. Philander runs behind the ball but isn't that quick enough. There was only a couple on offer but seeing the fielder's approach the batsmen cross for the third.
Stands tall in the crease and punches it down the ground.
Angles a length delivery from outside off, Smith gets across to defend but misses and is hit on the back pad.
Just short of a length ball on off, Usman punches it towards the man at point.
Outside off, knocked down to mid on.
Fuller and coming back in sharply, Khawaja leans forward for a mere push but gets it off the inner part of the bat towards mid on.
Short and outside off, Khawaja tries to cut by reaching out but fails to get going with the shot.
Outside off, left alone.
Khawaja hops and fends it towards covers.
The skipper, Steven Smith walks in next, replacing Warner!

OUT! That's really unlucky for David Warner! But South Africa wouldn't mind it at all. Abbott bangs in short on leg, Warner tries to defend but the ball hits the right thigh, pops up, then hits the right elbow and deflects on to the stumps. Warner is left stranded as he can't believe but to be frank he was nervy all throughout this innings. Australia lose both their openers and trail by 162 runs!
Outside off, sliced through point for a single.
Good length ball, moves away at the last moment. Khawaja tries to defend but gets a safe outside edge that dies well short of the man at gully.
Fuller in length on off, Warner pushes it past the non-striker towards mid off and scampers across for a quick single.
Touch full and around off, David once again blocks it out.
Fuller in length and around off, Warner lunges forward to defend.
On a length and around off, defended back to Kagiso.
Edged! Good length ball on off, Khawaja comes forward to defend but gets an outside edge towards gully where Duminy dives to his left to stop that one.
Fuller in length and outside off, Khawaja tries to drive this one through the off side but gets beaten all ends up.
Good length ball on off, Khawaja takes his bottom hand off as the ball bounces a bit more but still manages to defend it into the attack.
The rain has eased off and the action is all set to resume. The players scatter out on the field, Kagiso Rabada to finish his pending over...

That came all of a sudden. We have ANOTHER STOPPAGE DUE TO RAIN. No one realized it and suddenly, the batsmen were rushing for cover. Understandably, the Proteas are in no hurry to leave but they have to, because the drizzle is getting a bit heavier. But it is not that heavy and only the pitch is covered. Maybe only a short delay again.
Once again David taps it towards the off side. Duminy from gully and Bavuma from point give it a chase and it's the latter who gets to the ball. A single is taken.
Kagiso pitches it up on off, Warner comes forward and taps it towards Bavuma at point.
On a length and outside off, UK blocks it on the off side.
Stays deep in the crease and offers a straight bat.
Good length on the pads, nudged through square leg for a quick single.
Back of a length ball on off, bounces off the deck as Warner sees it passing through to the keeper.
Presses forward and offers a solid defense.

FOUR! Uppish but safe! Fuller in length and curling back in sharply. David Warner looks to drive it on the up but gets it off the outer part of the willow. It was in the air for a while but goes safely through point to the fence.
On a length and outside off, the batsman is happy to let one through.
Length ball on off, defended into the ground.
FOUR! Superbly driven! Very full outside off, Usman Khawaja leans into it and creams this one through covers for a boundary. Everything was perfect in that shot - stance, head position and timing!
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, UK hangs back in defense.
Short and outside off, Khawaja senses an opportunity to score as he gets back and cuts it but much to his dismay it goes straight to Bavuma at point.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot towards mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Almost a nick! Abbott is certainly troubling Warner here. Once again hurls it full outside off, David tries to defend it off the front foot but fails to get any wood on it.
Slants it away from Warner and tempts him to play at it. He accepts the proposal and the ball just beats the outside edge.
Fuller in length and angling in, Warner gets it off the inner part of the past mid-wicket for a couple.
Touch full and outside off, Warner lunges forward and defends it down gently. The ball rolls towards the bowler who fires a throw at the striker's end. It goes well over Warner to de Kock.
Fuller and strays it on the pads, Usman works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Angles in a length ball on middle and leg, Khawaja tucks it off his hips towards long leg for a single.
Stays back and pushes it towards mid on.
Back of a length ball outside off, Warner camps back and cracks it through cover-point and comes back for the third.
Touch short and outside off, David presses forward to defend but once again he gets beaten.

Edged but doesn't carry! Rabada is creating chances here. Fuller in length and angling in, Warner tries to defend it coming forward but gets a thickish outside edge which falls just short of Duminy at gully.

Beaten! Rabada comes steaming in from around the wicket and bowls it on a length around off. It straightens a touch as Warner tries to defend it without any foot movement. Gets beaten comprehensively.
Fuller in length and around off, Khawaja drives it towards short extra cover.
Comes forward and blocks it back towards Kyle.

A stifled appeal for a catch behind! Short and spraying down the leg side, Khawaja winds for the pull but misses as the ball kisses his thigh pads before de Kock collects it by swiftly moving to his right.
Good length delivery on off, defended gently off the back foot.
Fuller and hurled on the pads, Warner gets across and works it towards wide mid on for a single.
On a length and in the channel outside off, Warner prods forward to poke at it but is lucky not to nick it.
Did that hit the helmet? A bouncer on middle and leg, Khawaja takes his eyes off the ball and ducks but the ball goes off something to the keeper. Might have been helmet. There was a noise.
Landed around off, angling away, shouldered arms to.
Excellent variation. After bowling full for so long, Rabada suddenly bowls a yorker, on middle, Khawaja watches it closely and digs it out.
Full and outside off, pushed between cover and mid off for a run.
This is very straight, defended watchfully.
Full and on the pads, tucked towards fine leg for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and straight, defended watchfully.
Full on middle and leg, worked towards square leg.
Full and outside off, allowed to go through.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle and off, Khawaja is squared up a bit but manages to push it through the covers for a single.
Kyle Abbott to bowl from the other end!
Fuller in length and outside off, Warner drives it on the up past Philander at mid off who gives it a chase and keeps them down to a brace.
Good length ball on middle, getting some bounce on this one as DW gets back and turns it towards the leg side.
Fuller in length and around middle, Warner blocks it out.
Ripper! Back of a length ball, slanting across the batsmen. Warner tries to play it inside the line but the ball bounces a bit more and whizzes past the outside edge to the keeper.
An overpitched delivery on off, Warner gets on the front foot to drive off the carpet but finds short extra cover.
Starts off with a full length ball on off, Warner comes forward and jams it out towards mid off where Philander makes a diving stop. He seems to have hurt his right shoulder.
Welcome back for the final session of play. 33 overs left. Can Australia come out unscathed? Or will South Africa come out firing and keep picking up wickets? Here we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

Warner and Khawaja since then have been positive and seen Australia through to Tea. There have been some nervy moments for both the batsmen but so far it has been good for the hosts. The deficit is still 187 runs and they will know their job has just begun. South Africa have bowled well and will want to keep the pressure on Australia. Big last session coming up for both teams. Do join us for it in a short while.

That's a pretty good session for Australia, and we haven't said that before in this Test! They first cleaned up the South African tail with Hazlewood finishing with a six-wicket haul to bowl South Africa out for 326. Australia did lose Joe Burns though in the very first over before the heavens opened up again. At that stage, it seemed like a deja vu of the first innings was upon them. But it was not to be.
On middle and leg, Khawaja tucks it through square leg for a couple. TEA ON DAY 3!
Pushes this through the covers and gets a single. The deficit is now 189.
Outside off, left alone.

EDGED, BUT NOT TAKEN! FOUR! That is a lucky break for Warner. Back of a length outside off, Warner throws his bat at it but gets a top edge. The ball flies towards third slip but Dean Elgar does not pick it up at all and ducks to avoid getting hit. The ball races to the third man fence to bring up the 50 FOR AUSTRALIA. Faf du Plessis and Quinton de Kock are not too pleased with their mate.
Full and outside off, Warner pushes but misses.
Full and outside off, pushed past cover for a single.
KYLE ABBOTT to bowl the last over before Tea.
Looks to flick but gets it off the inside edge to fine leg. A single taken.
The batsman appears to have been struck on the thigh pad.
On middle and leg, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Very full outside off, squeezed behind point for a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Full on middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Kagiso Rabada is introduced into the attack. Can he strike before the Tea break?
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle and off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, Uzzie dead-bats it.
FOUR! Another fantastic shot. Tossed up outside off, Khawaja leans again and executes another perfect cover drive to move to 20 from 22 balls with his third boundary.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Elegant! Full and wide outside off, Khawaja leans into this one and drives it through the covers. Faf du Plessis dives over the ball at short extra cover but misses and it goes through.
Interesting. JP Duminy comes on to bowl with 8 minutes left to Tea.

Pitches this just short of a full length around leg and outside, David looks to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the thighs. Philander runs towards the keeper, half-appealing, half celebrating, thinking he has his man LBW but the umpire stays unmoved. No review taken this time. Perhaps height was the factor again.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Looks to tuck this to the leg side but misses and is hit on the pads.
Pushes this straight to cover point this time.
Short and outside off, punched on the bounce to gully.
Back of a length around off, flicked through square leg for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
FOUR! Crisp! Full and wide outside off, Warner reaches out and drives it through the covers for a boundary! The deficit is now 206. Warner moves to 23.
Full and on middle, watchfully defended.
On middle and leg, worked past square leg for a run.

KHAWAJA WAS A GONER HAD THAT HIT. Back of a length around middle and off, Warner gently opened the face of his bat and pushed it towards point. He immediately set off for the single but Khawaja was not that keen. He was then forced into the single and gave up. It was Temba Bavuma who ran from cover to his right but this time, he was not in a good position to throw the ball and missed the stumps at the striker's end by quite a distance.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
On middle and leg, flicked past square leg for a couple to end an eventful over.

NOT OUT! Height was the factor. Philander landed this on a length around middle and leg, Warner came forward to defend but missed and was hit on the pads. Philander was confident he had his man but umpire Richard Kettleborough did not agree. The bowler was adamant that this should be reviewed but his team mates were not that confident. De Kock was like, "Ummmm....maybe" while Amla was not too keen either. Faf du Plessis wanted to go with his keeper but in the end went with his bowler. Eagle Eye showed the ball to be going over the top.
Review time again! Philander reckons he has Warner trapped in front. Umpire Kettleborough has not agreed and Faf du Plessis takes the review.
On middle and leg, defended to the leg side.
Immediately Philander bowls this on middle, which means Warner has to play at it and he does, blocking it back to the bowler.
Landed around off, angling away, Warner comes forward, initially shows signs of wanting to play at that but then, at the last moment, takes his bat away.
Full and around middle, defended back to the bowler.
Full and around off, angling away, shouldered arms to again.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
On a good length outside off, comes back in, Khawaja looks to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the thigh pads.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and on middle and off, watchfully defended.

MISFIELD! He was brilliant on the previous ball, not quite so on this occasion. Warner gets across his stumps to a ball pitched full around off and pushes it straight to Kagiso Rabada at mid on. It is a pretty straightforward fielding attempt but perhaps the ball came quicker than his anticipation and he let it through his legs. Ran back towards the boundary to stop the ball from crossing the line and by that time the batsmen took three.
That is an outstanding stop. Full and wide outside off, Khawaja drives it through extra cover but Kagiso Rabada at mid off dives to his right and stops it cleanly.
Outside off, again in the avenue of apprehension, left alone.

Almost a reminiscence of his first innings dismissal. Philander lands this on a length just outside off, then gets it to nibble away. Khawaja is not sure whether to come forward or stay back and does neither. Has a tentative poke and misses.
On the pads, comfortably flicked towards backward square leg for a single.
Fuller in length, Warner drives it back to the bowler who mimes a throw at the stumps but the ball slips out of his hand.
Back of a length on middle and leg, pushed back to the bowler.
Landed wide outside off, left alone.
On middle and off, defended towards cover.
Comes around the wicket now...

That is just a push. The line is nice, just around off, forcing Warner to play. The length is good too, around full. The footwork is better from Warner, getting to the pitch of the ball. But the timing is outstanding as a mere push takes the ball almost to the long off fence. Three runs taken by the time Keshav Maharaj can get to the ball from cover. The deficit is now 219. Warner moves to 12.
Full and outside off, eased through the gap between cover and mid off for a couple.
Ummmm.... almost nicks it behind again. Full and wide outside off, Warner reaches out to drive but misses it completely. The ball carries nicely through to de Kock.
On middle and leg, worked past short leg. By the time Vernon Philander can get to the ball from backward square leg, the batsmen take three.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
A length ball around leg stump, worked straight to square leg.
Maintains that tight nagging line, outside off, David lets the ball through again.
Landed outside off, angling away, left alone.

Full and down the leg side, Warner misses his flick. Is this a plan by South Africa to get batsmen caught down the leg side? This is not the first ball in the innings in that direction. They already got Burns in that fashion. Whether it is happening because they are not able to control it or whether it is a plan, we will know only later.
On a good length around middle and leg, Warner misses his tuck and is hit right on the box.
FOUR! Caressed! Full and wide outside off, Khawaja comes forward and drives it through point to end the over with a boundary. The deficit is now 227.

Full and outside off, David leans and drives it through the covers. Keshav Maharaj and Temba Bavuma chase it in pairs and the former gets to the ball first, stops it from crossing the boundary and throws it to the keeper. Three runs taken.

BEATEN! That totally squared him up. Abbott is smiling. So is Warner. Just too good to get the batsman out. It was full and swinging away outside off, Warner was on the front foot to flick but was comprehensively beaten due to the late swing.
Outside off, left alone this time.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On middle and leg, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Goes right back in his crease and blocks.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On middle and leg, tucked through fine leg for a single. Leg bye signalled by the umpire.
Slips this down the leg side, DW lets it through and de Kock dives to his right to stop it.
Full and just outside off, David trusts the line and bounce and lets it go. The ball just goes past the off stump.

FOUR! Almost a replica of the first innings dismissal! Wow. Warner nearly, nearly gets sucked into the trap. The length is the same as was in the first innings. Just short of full. The line is wide as well, outside off. And instinctively, Warner goes after this one too. Only this time, he makes a slight adjustment. In the first innings, he attempted a full-blooded cover drive whereas now, he waited on the back foot and then got on top of the bounce and punched it through the covers.

Uzzie is off the mark. Fuller in length again, but on middle, Khawaja pushes it through mid on. The first call is "WAIT! WAIT!" as he expects Philander at mid-wicket to cut it off but the fielder does not take a start at all. The ball goes past him and now he starts running after the cherry. Accordingly, the batsmen run too and pick up a couple by the time Philander retrieves the ball.
Little bit of swing, but this is bowled on leg stump, Khawaja flicks it straight to short mid-wicket.
The players are out in the middle. USMAN KHAWAJA joins David Warner at the crease. Abbott to complete his over. Pressure right on Australia!
0910 IST - The rain has relented, no respite for Australia. Play to resume at 0920 IST. Tea will be taken at 1010 IST. We have a lot of overs left for the day.

Oh dear! The rain is back and the players are off the field. Burns would be feeling terribly unlucky, if only he had seen off that ball. Australia are up against it here. Stay tuned, let's hope the weather clears up soon.

OUT! The decision is overturned! Burns departs for a duck! Abbott bowls it full but on middle and leg, Burns looks to clip it but does not connect properly. There is a noise as the ball goes past the bat. de Kock goes to his left, collects the ball and starts celebrating. He cannot believe it is not given out. Faf goes for the review straightaway. The replays show there was a tiny mark on HotSpot and the Snicko too confirms the edge and that is curtains for Joe Burns. He was walking away when Faf opted for the review. South Africa have begun superbly here.
There is a massive appeal for a catch down the leg side! Burns has been given not out but South Africa have reviewed it.
On a length outside off, left alone by Burns.
Fuller outside off, swings away, Burns lets it go through easily.
Starts off with a fuller one on off, Burns keeps it out. There was a hint of swing on that one.
